# New renderings chosen in odyssey-115 (24.1–105)

Each is a formula or epithet that is likely to recur. Columns follow the conventions table: Greek, `l`, `i`, avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀκάκητα (Hermes, 24.10; meaning unknown, ancient guess 'giver of no harm') | "Akakêta" | "the Harmless" (+ note: unknown; guess from ἀ- + κακός) | "the kindly", "the unharming", "the gentle" (each silently picks the guess) |
| εὐρώεντα κέλευθα (24.10) | "the dank ways" | "the dank ways" | "mouldy", "the dark paths", "the damp roads"; κέλευθα keeps the table's "ways" |
| Λευκὰς πέτρη (24.11, Λευκάδα πέτρην) | "the White Rock" | "the White Rock" | "the Leucadian rock", "the rock Leucas" (the place is not identified in the text) |
| Ἠελίοιο πύλαι (24.12) | "the gates of the Sun" | "the gates of the Sun" | "the gates of Helios", "the sun-gates" |
| δῆμος ὀνείρων (24.12) | "the land of dreams" | "the land of dreams" | "the people of dreams", "the realm of dreams"; keeps the table's δῆμος "land" |
| εἴδωλα καμόντων (24.14) | "phantoms of those who have toiled" | "the phantoms of those who have finished toiling" | "ghosts of the dead", "images of the weary" (the euphemism of καμόντες is kept) |
| τὸν (δ’ αὖτε) ψυχὴ προσεφώνεε(ν) + genitive of a patronymic (whole-line speech introduction, 24.23, 24.35, 24.105) | "Him first the soul of the son of Peleus spoke to:" / "Him in turn the soul of Atreus’ son spoke to:" / "Him first the soul of Atreus’ son spoke to:" | "The soul of the son of Peleus spoke to him first:" / "The soul of the son of Atreus spoke to him in turn:" / "The soul of the son of Atreus spoke to him first:" | "addressed" (reserved for προσέειπε / προσέφη), "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); προσεφώνεε keeps "spoke to" as in the table; προτέρη is "first" |
| θεοῖς ἐπιείκελος (24.36) | "resembling the gods" | "like the gods" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος), "equal to the gods", "divine" (reserved for θεῖος); follows the table’s ἐπιείκελος ἀθανάτοισιν (15.414) "resembling the immortals" / "like the immortals" |
| ἀθανάτῃς ἁλίῃσιν (24.47, 24.55; fem. dative plural, nymphs of the sea) | "the immortal sea-ones" | "the immortal goddesses of the sea" | "sea-nymphs", "Nereids" (neither word is in the Greek), "immortal maidens of the brine" |
| παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς (24.51, of Nestor) | "knowing things old and many" | "who knew things old and many" | "full of old wisdom", "of long experience", "who knew many ancient things" |
| οὗ καὶ πρόσθεν ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή (24.52, of Nestor) | "whose counsel earlier too appeared best" | "whose counsel had also seemed best before" | "wisest", "his plan proved best" |
| θερμὰ δάκρυα (24.45–46) | "hot tears" | "hot tears" | "warm tears" (kept for λιαρός), "burning tears" |
| ἄμβροτα εἵματα (24.59) | "deathless garments" | "deathless garments" | follows the table's ἄμβροτος "deathless" |
| ἔσχοντο φόβου (24.57) | "held back from flight" | "stopped short of flight" | "stopped being afraid" (φόβος here is the fear that sends men running; the note says so) |
| ἀργυρόπεζα Θέτις (24.92) | "silver-footed Thetis" | "silver-footed Thetis" | "silver-ankled", "silver-slippered" (πέζα is 'foot') |
| ἱερὸς στρατός (24.81) | "the sacred host" | "the sacred host" | "holy host" (reserved for ἠγάθεος), "sacred army", "the divine host"; follows the table’s ἱερός "sacred" |
| περικαλλέ’ ἄεθλα (24.85, 24.91; prizes) beside ἄεθλα (24.89; contests) | "very fair contest-prizes" / "the contests" | "very fair contest-prizes" / "the contests" | "prizes" alone (loses that they are won in a contest), "games"; follows the table's ἄεθλον "contest" and ἀέθλια "contest-prizes" |
| ἀριστήεσσιν Ἀχαιῶν (24.86) | "the best of the Achaeans" | "the best of the Achaeans" | "the chieftains", "the champions" |
| καλὸν χρόα (24.44) | "fine skin" | "fine skin" | "fair skin" (kept for κάλλιμος, περικαλλής), "beautiful flesh" |
